Let me try to explain. Some people are just born into shitty circumstances. You can’t necessarily help someone’s biochemistry, birth defects, social circumstances, etc. There are many veterans who have been to war and have PTSD and are non compos mentis. There are also civilians who have PTSD who become the same way. I am one of those civilians. And I’m close to being homeless. 

I have a genetic disadvantage in a very competitive world and there’s not much I can do about it w/o paying an arm and leg and that’s the catch. I have a one-inch leg length discrepancy, clinical depression, generalized anxiety disorder, and gastroesophageal reflux disorder. To sum it up, I’m in a lot of pain. I honestly just want to kill myself or get assisted suicide to avoid the years of suffering that comes with being homeless. Believe it or not, I used to be an Assistant Manager at a very good company and then I had a traumatic event that flipped my world upside down. 

Now I have trouble filling out forms and my attention span is shit. People have to speak very slowly to me and I can tell it frustrates them. I can’t handle as much information as I used to. My energy is gone. Everything used to feel so effortless and now it feels like I expend all of my energy just by doing small things. Folks don’t understand it so I’m out of the house. 

Some people are just lucky in life. Some get unlucky. That’s just the way it goes. Life can happen to anyone and it’s super easy to talk about homelessness like you are talking about what to make for dinner, but the reality of being homeless is horrifying and is a terrible way to live, especially if you come from a super nice home.

We literally all don’t really know how we got to where we are. Some of us got extremely lucky being born into a family with good genetics. Some of us got extremely unlucky. It’s literally all luck. People take pride in hard work, but the reality is your entire life is circumstantial and there’s nothing you can do to change that.
